data.body:
Phase 1 RCA / not-a-bug classification (2026-08-18)

Reproduction: from a fresh git repo with an isolated temporary HOME/XDG config and no identity tickets, `rebar init --force-new-store` created `.tickets-tracker/.env-id` and `.signing-key`. `rebar create task ...` succeeded with unsigned authorship under the default/advisory posture. The first direct attestation operation, `rebar sign <ticket> ["probe: PASS"]`, succeeded, lazily created `.opcert-key` + `.opcert-key.pub`, and `rebar verify-signature` returned `verified=true`, `verdict=certified`. `.rebar/current_identity` remained absent and `rebar list --type identity` was empty. Thus gate/op-cert signing does not require an author identity or `identity create --self`.

Confirmed mechanism: gate attestations use an environment identity and op-cert key, not the authenticated-authorship identity. `src/rebar/_commands/init.py:223-310,646-661` mints the store `.env-id`; `src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:31-34,156-205,209-225,270-330` lazily generates the Ed25519 op-cert key on first signing and uses `.env-id` as principal. Author identities are a separate optional write-signing system: `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:307-410` requires a resolvable identity + `identity.signing_key` only when `identity.require_authenticated` is enabled for a non-exempt ticket event; `rebar.toml:112-140` currently sets that posture false in this repository.

Discriminating experiment: setting `REBAR_IDENTITY_REQUIRE_AUTHENTICATED=true` made an ordinary task CREATE fail with the documented missing-authorship error. The literal proposed command `rebar identity create --self` itself failed because CLI syntax also requires `--name` and `--email` (`src/rebar/_commands/identity.py:559-660`). Creating an identity with name/email and `--self` still left the next enforced write failing with `no identity.signing_key configured`. This rules out the report’s proposed one-line remediation as sufficient. In an enforced project the correct flow is conditional: create a new identity with its public key only when none exists, otherwise `rebar identity use <id>` or rely on the unique git-email match, and configure the matching private `identity.signing_key`. `docs/identity-setup.md:12-49,60-74,143-173` and `docs/identity.md:169-195` already document that complete contract; `docs/local-dev-env.md:84-91` points local contributors to it, and `docs/README.md:36-39` indexes the client setup guide.

Defect legitimacy: `misunderstanding`, not a defect. The claimed clean-onboarding gate failure is contradicted by runtime reproduction and the op-cert implementation. Authenticated authorship is intentionally opt-in (`docs/identity.md:129-156`); gate attestations intentionally self-bootstrap environment signing. Adding an unconditional `identity create --self` prerequisite to AGENTS/setup would conflate two identity systems, duplicate existing identities, omit the required public/private key setup, and incorrectly burden projects with advisory authorship. No code or docs were edited.

Recommended disposition: close as not-a-bug. If the client’s real concern is discoverability of optional authenticated-authorship setup from AGENTS.md, treat that as a separately approved documentation enhancement with wording that explicitly distinguishes author-event signing from gate op-certs and says create-or-reuse, never unconditional create.
